title: Online and Survey Representations of Well-Being: Coherence and Cross-Source Correspondence
abstract: arXiv:2611.08510v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Digital traces may complement population surveys in the measurement of well-being, but the two sources do not necessarily capture identical constructs. We compare the Human Flourishing Geographic Index (HFGI) with World Values Survey and European Social Survey measures across three domains using structural equation models. The results show strong within-source coherence and construct-specific cross-source correspondence. Cross-source convergence varies across domains; the observed pattern is consistent with stronger correspondence where the underlying indicators are more closely aligned conceptually. Near-perfect agreement would be unexpected, since surveys elicit standardized self-reports, whereas HFGI captures naturally occurring public expressions. HFGI should therefore be viewed as a distinct but empirically connected measurement system that complements survey-based evidence on well-being.

translated_title: 幸福感的在线表征与调查表征：内部一致性与跨来源对应关系
translated_abstract: 数字痕迹可以在幸福感的测量中对人口调查起到补充作用，但这两种数据来源未必捕捉到相同的构念。我们使用结构方程模型，在三个领域中比较了人类繁荣地理指数与来自世界价值观调查和欧洲社会调查的测量指标。结果显示，两种来源内部均具有很强的一致性，而跨来源的对应关系则因构念而异。跨来源的收敛程度在不同领域之间存在差异；所观察到的模式表明，当底层指标在概念上更为接近时，对应关系更强。近乎完全的一致本就难以预期，因为调查获取的是标准化的自我报告，而HFGI捕捉的是自然产生的公开表达。因此，HFGI应被视为一个独特但在实证上相互关联的测量系统，它能够补充基于调查的幸福感证据。
tldr: 本研究通过结构方程模型比较人类繁荣地理指数（HFGI）与世界价值观调查和欧洲社会调查数据，发现两者各自内部具有高度一致性，跨来源对应关系因构念而异且在指标概念更接近的领域更强，表明HFGI是与调查证据互补的独特但实证相关的幸福感测量系统。
en_tdlr: This study uses structural equation models to compare the Human Flourishing Geographic Index (HFGI) with World Values Survey and European Social Survey measures, finding strong within-source coherence and construct-specific cross-source correspondence that is stronger where indicators align conceptually, positioning HFGI as a distinct but empirically connected measurement system that complements survey-based well-being evidence.
